key_insight: HVAF spraying can produce thick NiTi coatings that retain martensitic transformation and shape-memory functionality after post-annealing, despite significant as-sprayed defects.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to add functional, thermally responsive NiTi surfaces on steel components for actuation, smart repair, or adaptive wear-protection applications.
method: HVAF-sprayed NiTi onto mild steel using four processing parameter sets.
Characterized composition, porosity, microstructure, phase transformation, and thermomechanical behavior.
Evaluated functional response with 3-point bending, nanoindentation, and scratch testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that 100–300 μm coatings showed martensitic transformation and measurable thermal actuation/shape memory behavior after annealing, with good substrate adhesion.
watch_item: As-sprayed coatings are microstructurally inhomogeneous and defect-rich, so annealing and process control are critical to achieve reliable functional performance.
paper_title: HVAF Spraying of NiTi Coatings: Microstructure, Phase Transformation and Shape Memory Behavior
